neatHack · Oct 10–12, 2026 · working name

Upshiftv0.1.0

Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass.

An agent that keeps a Python codebase current. It patches vulnerable packages, upgrades frameworks and the Python runtime, and follows third-party APIs when they change version. It reads the docs, rewrites the code that breaks, and proves the result with your own tests.

upshift/maintenance · 3 jobs · tests 212 passed, 0 new failures
- pydantic==1.10.2            # CVE-2024-3772+ pydantic==2.9.2- requires-python = ">=3.10"+ requires-python = ">=3.12"- POST https://api.acme.dev/v1/charges   # Sunset: 2026-11-01+ POST https://api.acme.dev/v2/payments  # Idempotency-Key added  38 files changed · playbook: 41 cited rules · $0.84 · 11m 20s
The problem

Bumping a version takes one line. Fixing what breaks takes a week.

Dependabot and Renovate tell you a package is out of date or vulnerable, then hand you a PR with red CI. Major upgrades sit untouched for months, Python versions fall behind, and an API provider's deprecation notice gets noticed when production starts returning 410s. The hard part is the migration work in between: reading changelogs, finding every call site, and fixing them without breaking anything else.

Three triggers, one engine

What starts a job

Vulnerability
Detects
pip-audit against the OSV database. Dependabot alerts too, when the repo is on GitHub.
Researches
The advisory, the smallest fixed version, and the changelog between versions.
$ upshift scan --repo .
Developer asks
Detects
A request to bump a package or the Python runtime itself.
Researches
Migration guides, release notes and an API diff between the two installed versions. For Python, the "What's New" docs and removed stdlib modules.
$ upshift bump --python 3.12
API drift
Detects
Deprecation and Sunset headers, 410s and "deprecated" warnings in neatlogs traces and app logs.
Researches
The provider's new docs and OpenAPI spec, diffed against the version in use.
$ upshift watch --neatlogs
How a job runs

The engine

Every trigger produces the same kind of job and goes through the same steps. Nothing in the engine is specific to one framework.

  1. ResearchFetch changelogs, migration guides and specs. Diff the old and new APIs directly.
  2. PlaybookDistil rules of the form "old pattern → new pattern", each with a source link. Cached for the next repo.
  3. BaselineRun the tests before changing anything, so failures that already existed don't count.
  4. PlanFind every affected call site with entire-graph and order fixes by blast radius.
  5. Fix loopBump, run tests, group failures, fix one group at a time with Claude.
  6. RecoverRetry throttles, revert regressions, re-plan with the error, or split out a sub-job.
  7. VerifyNo new test failures, advisory cleared, no deprecated APIs left.
  8. ShipA branch, a report with sources and cost, and a PR description.

State is saved after every step and each fixed group is its own commit, so a crashed or killed run resumes where it stopped.

Demo

One neglected app, three fixes

shop_app runs on Python 3.10, pins vulnerable packages, uses Pydantic v1, and calls a mock payments API that is about to retire v1.

$ upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app
  3 advisories · jinja2, werkzeug, pydantic → fixed, 0 new test failures
$ upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --python 3.12
  removed distutils usage · 2 deps bumped for 3.12 wheels · tests pass on 3.12
$ acme-mock --mode deprecating && python -m shop_app
$ upshift watch --repo demo/shop_app --neatlogs
  acme v1 deprecated (Sunset 2026-11-01) · fetched v2 spec · 6 call sites migrated
$ acme-mock --mode sunset && python -m shop_app
  orders processed via /v2/payments

The bench also runs on small open-source repos across at least three migrations (Pydantic 1→2, SQLAlchemy 1.4→2.0, a Python bump) to show that it generalises. Output above is the target, not a recorded run.

Required stack

How we use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai

neatlogs

observability
  • Every run is traced: one span per job, per phase and per tool call, with tokens, cost, latency, retries and recovery decisions.
  • The agent is also an MCP client of neatlogs. It searches app traces for failing or deprecated API calls, which is how API drift gets detected.
  • We benchmark v0, find waste and failure patterns through the neatlogs MCP, fix them, and compare v1 on the same repos.
  • Measured cost per job becomes the cost input for the business plan.

Entire

repo context
  • Our own repo has Entire enabled, so each commit links to the Claude Code session that wrote it.
  • Inside the agent, entire-graph is the code-intelligence layer: search finds affected code, impact orders fixes, explain adds declarations to test failures.
  • entire graph verify with a recorded baseline is the gate that separates new failures from old ones.

cfo.ai

business plan
  • Pricing: a per-repo monthly subscription, plus a per-job charge for major migrations.
  • Costs come from real neatlogs numbers per job type, plus compute and headcount.
  • Base and upside revenue scenarios with runway, built with Ari and shared as a read-only report.
Definition of done

What has to be true

  • Each trigger completes end to end on shop_app with no new test failures against the baseline.
  • At least two different framework migrations pass on real repos with no framework-specific code.
  • Every playbook rule cites its source, and a second repo on the same migration reuses the cached playbook.
  • A killed run resumes and finishes without redoing completed work.
  • neatlogs shows a failure the agent recovered from, plus v0 vs v1 numbers on the same bench.
  • Commits carry Entire checkpoints, and the cfo.ai plan covers pricing, costs, revenue and runway.
48 hours

Roadmap

Sat, Oct 10

Engine

  • Repo, Entire, neatlogs and Bedrock set up
  • Research → fix → verify on one package bump
  • Day 1 post
Sun, Oct 11

Triggers

  • Recovery, resume, verification gate
  • Vulnerability scan and Python bump
  • API drift with mock API and neatlogs detection
  • Bench v0, improve, cfo.ai plan
Mon, Oct 12

Ship

  • Bench v1 and compare
  • README with evidence, demo video
  • Submit, 7:00–11:55 PM IST
Cut lineIf API drift isn't working by Sunday 9 PM, it detects from local logs only and demos the deprecation stage.
Built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Claude on Amazon Bedrock. python only · v0.1 plan

Tool showcase

Where every tool shows up

Each tool is used at more than one stage: while we build Upshift, while Upshift runs, while we improve it, and in the evidence we submit.

ToolBuilding UpshiftInside the agentImproving itSubmission evidence
neatlogsrequired MCP server in Claude Code to read our traces while we code Traces every job, phase and tool call. MCP client that detects API drift in app traces v0 bench → find waste and failures → fix → v1 bench Trace links, v0 vs v1 numbers, a recovery trace
Entirerequired Checkpoints link every commit to the Claude Code session that wrote it entire-graph finds affected code, orders fixes and gates verification checkpoint explain to see why a change was made before reworking it entire checkpoint list, commit trailers, graph spans in traces
cfo.airequired n/a n/a Re-run the model with v1 cost per job to show margin improving Business plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway, shared link
AWS Bedrockcredits n/a Claude via the Converse API for research, playbooks and fixes Swap model per phase if traces show a cheaper one is enough Model calls visible in traces with token cost
Claude Codebuilder Writes Upshift, with entire-graph guidance and neatlogs MCP n/a Reads trace analysis and applies fixes Sessions captured as Entire checkpoints

neatlogs

trace, detect, improve
  1. Instrument the agent. Initialise before boto3 is imported, so every Bedrock call carries tokens, cost and latency. Each phase and tool gets its own span. 
    # upshift/__init__.py
neatlogs.init(workflow_name="upshift",
              tags=[AGENT_VERSION, job.kind, job.repo],
              instrumentations=["bedrock"])

@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="graph_impact")
def graph_impact(symbol): ...

with neatlogs.trace("verify", kind="GUARDRAIL") as span:
    span.set_attribute("upshift.new_failures", n)
  2. Detect API drift. The demo app is traced too. Upshift connects to the neatlogs MCP server and searches those traces for 410s and deprecation headers. 
    search_traces(query="acme 410 OR Deprecation OR Sunset")
get_trace_context(trace_id)  # headers, endpoint, code location
list_detections()            # error-rate spikes on acme calls
  3. Improve with evidence. In Claude Code, the neatlogs MCP shows where v0 loops, retries or sends oversized context. We fix those, rerun the same bench as v1, and compare. 
    $ npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key $NEATLOGS_API_KEY
$ upshift bench --tag v0   # then fix, then
$ upshift bench --tag v1

Entire

repo context, for us and the agent
  1. Capture how Upshift was built. Every commit gets an Entire-Checkpoint trailer linking it to the Claude Code session that produced it. 
    $ entire enable --agent claude-code
$ entire plugin install graph
$ entire graph init-agents   # graph guidance in CLAUDE.md
  2. Give the agent a map of the code. Upshift calls entire-graph to find what a migration touches and to fix the most-depended-on code first. 
    $ entire graph search --repo . --query "acme charges client" --format json
$ entire graph impact --repo . --symbol AcmeClient.create_charge
$ pytest 2>&1 | entire graph explain --repo .
  3. Prove nothing new broke. A baseline is recorded before any change, so only failures the migration caused count against it. 
    $ entire graph verify --repo . --test "pytest -q" --record-baseline base.json
# ... upgrade and fix ...
$ entire graph verify --repo . --test "pytest -q" --pre-edit-baseline base.json

cfo.ai

the business behind the agent
  1. Feed in real unit costs. Cost per job type (vuln fix, package bump, Python bump, API migration) comes straight from neatlogs, not guesses.
  2. Build the model with Ari. An example of what we ask, with the numbers filled in from our bench: 
    Model a developer-tools startup selling Upshift.
Pricing: per-repo monthly subscription, plus a per-job fee for major migrations.
COGS per job from neatlogs: vuln fix $__, package bump $__, API migration $__.
Show base and upside scenarios for 24 months with headcount and runway.
  3. Ship the plan. Share a read-only report from cfo.ai and export the summary into business/plan.md in the repo.

# neatHack plan: autonomous dependency & API upkeep agent (working name `upshift`)

## Context
neatHack (48h, Oct 10 12:30 PM → Oct 12 11:55 PM IST) asks for an agent that completes a substantial task end-to-end. It must use **neatlogs**, **Entire** and **cfo.ai**, with checkable evidence for each. Judging: agent 30%, tool use 25%, demo 20%, building in public 15%, originality 10%.

**What the agent does:** it keeps a Python repo current, fixing the code that breaks, not just opening bump PRs the way Dependabot does. **One engine, three triggers:**

| Trigger | Detects | Researches | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Vuln** | `pip-audit` (OSV) JSON; Dependabot alerts via `gh api` when the repo is on GitHub | Advisory + changelog between versions | jinja2 CVE → fixed version |
| **Bump** (developer asks) | `upshift bump --package X --to Y` or `--python 3.12` | Package: PyPI links, changelog, releases, API diff. Python: "What's New" per minor version, removed stdlib modules, dependency compatibility | Pydantic 1→2; Python 3.10→3.12 |
| **API drift** | App logs + neatlogs traces: `Deprecation`/`Sunset`/`Link: rel=successor-version` headers, 410/4xx bursts, "deprecated" warnings | The provider's new docs / OpenAPI spec, diffed against the old one | acme API v1 → v2 |

Every trigger produces a **Job** that goes through the same pipeline: **research → cited playbook → plan → fix loop → recover → verify → branch + PR**.

**Decisions made:**
- Claude on **Bedrock** (AWS credits)
- Custom Python loop
- Python ecosystem only
- Priority: engine + bump + vuln first, API drift last
- Logs: neatlogs traces + local log files
- API-drift demo: a mock API we control
- Vuln source: pip-audit, with Dependabot optional

`/Users/harsh/agent-101/neatlogs-agent` is empty, so this is greenfield. It must become a **public** repo with commits dated inside the event. The repo name is open (see the end).

---

## Pipeline (shared engine)
CLI commands:
- `upshift scan --repo R` (vuln)
- `upshift bump --repo R (--package P [--to V] | --python 3.12)`
- `upshift watch --repo R [--logs PATH] [--neatlogs]` (API drift)
- `upshift resume <run_id>`
- `upshift bench`

1. **Trigger → Job** `{kind, target, evidence}`.
   - **Vuln:** pick the *smallest* fixed version, preferring the same major version. Only a major jump goes through the full migration path.
   - **Python bump:** run `uv pip compile --python-version 3.12` to find dependencies that won't resolve. Each becomes a sub-job through the same engine.
2. **Research → playbook.** A list of rules (old pattern → new pattern), each with its source URL, cached in `playbooks/`.
   - **Package:** PyPI JSON → changelog/docs/source links → migration guide and release notes. An **API diff** installs both versions in temp venvs (`uv`) and compares public symbols and signatures with `inspect`. It's the ground truth when docs are thin.
   - **Python:** `docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.11.html`, `3.12.html`, and so on. Removed modules (`distutils`, `imp`, `asynchat`…). Config surfaces to update: `requires-python`, `.python-version`, Dockerfile `FROM`, CI matrix, tox.
   - **API:** follow the `Link` successor URL / configured docs URL → fetch the old and new OpenAPI specs → diff endpoints, params, fields and auth headers.
3. **Setup.** Clone into `workspaces/<run_id>`, then `uv venv` (with the target Python if needed) and install. Record the test baseline with `entire graph verify --test "pytest -q" --record-baseline`.
4. **Plan.** Find affected code with `entire graph search`/`symbols` plus grep for playbook APIs (for API drift: the host/URL/client methods). Order the work by blast radius with `entire graph impact`.
5. **Apply the bump / config change**, run the tests, and group the failures by root cause.
6. **Fix loop** (Claude tool-use, one failure group at a time). Tools: `read_file`, `edit_file`, `run_tests`, `graph_impact`, `graph_explain`, `search_code`, `lookup_playbook` and `fetch_docs`. New findings are added back to the playbook. A group that passes is committed; a regression means reverting that file.
7. **Recover.** Classify each failure and pick a strategy:
   - Bedrock throttle → backoff and retry.
   - Bad edit → re-read the file and retry.
   - Regression → revert and re-plan with the error in context.
   - Install conflict → relax or pin, or spawn a sub-job.
   - Budget cap (iterations, tokens, $) → stop with a partial report.
8. **State.** Write `.upshift/state.json` and make a git commit per fixed group, so `resume` survives a crash or kill.
9. **Verify** (a `GUARDRAIL` span).
   - `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` must report no new failures.
   - Vuln: `pip-audit` is clean for that advisory.
   - Bump: tests run with deprecation warnings as errors, and no old APIs from the playbook remain.
   - API drift: tests pass against the new API version, and a re-run shows no deprecation signals.
10. **Output.** A branch `upshift/<kind>-<target>`, `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` (changes, playbook citations, what's left, cost) and a PR body (`gh pr create` is optional).

## Demo setup (one story, all three triggers)
- **`demo/acme_api/`**: a FastAPI mock third-party API.
  - `/v1/charges` has modes `ok → deprecating → sunset`. "Deprecating" sends `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` headers; "sunset" returns 410.
  - `/v2/payments` renames fields (`amount` → `amount_cents`), requires an `Idempotency-Key` header, and nests the response.
  - It serves `/v1/openapi.json`, `/v2/openapi.json` and `/docs/migration`.
- **`demo/shop_app/`**: a deliberately neglected app.
  - Python 3.10, vulnerable pins (e.g. old jinja2/werkzeug), Pydantic v1, and calls to acme v1.
  - Instrumented with neatlogs (acme calls wrapped as `TOOL` spans that record status codes and headers), writing to `logs/app.log`.
  - Has pytest tests that run against the mock.
- **Demo flow:** `scan` fixes the CVEs → `bump --python 3.12` → put the mock in "deprecating" mode and run the app → `watch` sees the drift in neatlogs and the logs, then migrates to v2 → switch the mock to "sunset" mode and the app still works.
- **`evals/repos.yaml`**: shop_app plus 3–4 small real OSS repos (Pydantic 1→2, SQLAlchemy 1.4→2.0, one Python bump), pinned to fixed commits.

## Files to create
```
pyproject.toml                       # neatlogs[anthropic], boto3, mcp, pip-audit, typer, pyyaml, httpx
upshift/cli.py                       # scan | bump | watch | resume | bench
upshift/jobs.py                      # Job model
upshift/triggers/{vuln,bump,api_drift}.py
upshift/research/{package,python,api,playbook}.py
upshift/engine/{agent,tools,recovery,state}.py
upshift/llm.py                       # Bedrock Converse wrapper (model id via env)
upshift/graph.py                     # subprocess wrappers over `entire graph ...`
upshift/neatlogs_mcp.py              # MCP client → search_traces / list_detections / get_trace_context
upshift/prompts/
playbooks/                           # cached cited playbooks
demo/acme_api/, demo/shop_app/
evals/repos.yaml, evals/bench.py
business/                            # cfo.ai export
hackathon.md, README.md              # build log + evidence table
```

---

## How each required tool is used

### neatlogs: observe and improve the agent, *and* a detection source
1. **Tracing the agent.**
   - `neatlogs.init(workflow_name="upshift", tags=[agent_version, job_kind, repo], instrumentations=["bedrock"])` before importing boto3.
   - Spans: `WORKFLOW` per job, `AGENT` per phase (research/plan/fix/verify), `TOOL` per tool (including every `entire graph` call), `GUARDRAIL` for verify.
   - `set_attribute` for state transitions, failure class, retries and recovery strategy.
   - `identify` sets session = run_id, so resumed runs stay together.
   - `flush()`/`shutdown()` on exit.
2. **Detection for API drift.** The agent is an **MCP client of neatlogs** (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`). It calls `search_traces` / `list_detections` / `get_trace_context` on the shop_app project to find failing or deprecated acme calls, and falls back to local logs. This matches the hackathon's "watch a running system" example.
3. **Improvement loop.**
   - Run `bench` as v0.
   - In Claude Code, use the neatlogs MCP (`triage_list`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`) to find waste and failure patterns. Fix them, then run v1.
   - Compare success rate, iterations, tokens, $ per job and wall time.
4. **Recovery evidence** comes from real failure traces (throttles, bad edits, regressions, install conflicts).
5. **Unit cost** per job type, as measured in neatlogs, feeds cfo.ai.

### Entire: context for us *and* the agent
1. **On our repo.**
   - `entire enable --agent claude-code` adds checkpoint trailers that link each commit to the Claude Code session that wrote it. This is the evidence, and it proves the code was written during the event.
   - `entire graph init-agents` gives Claude Code graph guidance while we build.
2. **Inside the agent.** entire-graph is its code-intelligence layer:
   - `search`/`symbols` → find usages of the affected APIs and third-party call sites
   - `impact`/`neighbors` → order fixes by blast radius
   - `explain` → pipe pytest failures in to get the relevant declarations
   - `verify` with record/pre-edit baselines → the verification gate

### cfo.ai: the business plan
1. Model "autonomous dependency & API upkeep" with Ari:
   - **Pricing:** per-repo/month subscription plus per-job overage for major migrations.
   - **COGS:** neatlogs $ per job type plus compute.
   - **Opex/headcount**, base/upside **revenue scenarios**, **runway**.
   - **Positioning:** Dependabot/Renovate open bump PRs but leave the breakage to you. Snyk fixes vulnerabilities only. Upshift fixes the code, including drift in runtime APIs.
2. Share a read-only page link and export to `business/plan.md`. Cancel cfo.ai billing right after signup.

| Agent improved | v0 vs v1 neatlogs trace links + bench table |
| Used neatlogs | trace links, the agent's MCP detection calls, MCP-driven fixes logged in `hackathon.md` |

- **Oct 11, morning.** Recovery, state/resume, verify gate. **Vuln trigger** (pip-audit → Job). **Python bump** (uv + whatsnew + dependency sub-jobs). Post #2.
- **Oct 11, afternoon/evening.**
  - **API drift:** acme mock, shop_app, log + neatlogs MCP detection, OpenAPI diff → fix.
  - v0 bench → neatlogs analysis → v1.
  - cfo.ai plan. Post #3.
- **Oct 12 (until ~6 PM).** v1 bench, README evidence, ~3-minute video (the demo flow above plus traces plus cfo.ai). Submit 7:00–11:55 PM.
- **Cut line:** if API drift isn't working by Oct 11 at 9 PM, use local-log detection only (drop the neatlogs MCP detection) and demo only the "deprecating" mode.

## Risks to check first
- How well entire-graph handles Python (`entire graph capabilities --json`). Fallback: grep + `ast` for search/impact.
- Whether neatlogs `bedrock` auto-instrumentation catches boto3 `converse`. Fallback: `neatlogs.wrap(client)`.
- Whether the neatlogs MCP can search non-LLM `TOOL` spans by attribute (status code/headers) for shop_app. Fallback: local logs.
- Bedrock model access/region (env-configurable). `uv python install 3.12` works offline-ish.
- Huge changelogs. Cap text per source, rely on the API/OpenAPI diff as truth, and cite every rule.

## Verification
- `upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app` → `pip-audit` comes back clean for the fixed advisories, with no new test failures.
- `upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --python 3.12` → tests pass in a 3.12 venv; `requires-python`, Dockerfile and CI are updated.
- `upshift bump --package pydantic --to 2` on bench repos → `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` shows zero new failures. At least 2 different frameworks pass with no framework-specific code.
- Mock in "deprecating" mode → run shop_app → `upshift watch --neatlogs` detects acme v1 → migrates to v2 → tests pass against v2. With the mock in "sunset" mode, the app still works.
- Kill mid-run, then `upshift resume <id>` → finishes without redoing completed groups.
- neatlogs shows WORKFLOW→AGENT→TOOL spans with tokens and cost, and v0/v1 can be filtered by tag. `git log` has `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.

## Repo name (open)
Not prescribed by the hackathon. Still fits: **`upshift`** (recommended), `bumpbot`, `keepcurrent`, `driftfix`.

entire graph adds a deterministic, no-egress code graph to Entire checkpoints.

Usage:
  entire graph <command> [flags]

Set up your agent:
  init-agents      Install the coding-agent guide into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
  agent-guide      Print the coding-agent operating guide
  index            Build/warm a committed-tree cache variant for matching queries
  capabilities     List parsed languages, relation types, and features

Inspect the graph:
  search           Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)
  neighbors        Who calls this / what does it call (targeted relations)
  impact           One-shot blast radius for changing a symbol
  def              What a name IS: declaration, fields, and method surface
  explain          Resolve symbols named by a failing build or test
  symbols          Stream every symbol definition (bulk NDJSON)
  edges            Stream every relation (bulk NDJSON)
  snapshot         Stream the whole graph: files, symbols, and relations (bulk NDJSON)
  snapshot-query   Query a compact snapshot without rebuilding the graph

Analyze changes & more:
  commit           Entity-level change list for a commit vs its first parent
  diff             Entity-level change list between two refs
  checkpoint       Analyze the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
  verify           Run a test command and return an adjudicated verdict, not test output
  stats            Human report: graph usage vs grep/read, and estimated token savings

Help & diagnostics:
  help             Show this command listing
  doctor           Diagnose the environment and confirm no-egress
  version          Print the plugin version (and provider name with --json)

---
Run a test command and return an adjudicated verdict, not test output

Usage:
  entire graph verify --test "<cmd>" --repo . [--setup "<cmd>"] [--record-baseline path | --pre-edit-baseline path] [--max-bytes 2048]

verify runs your test command and reports WHICH TESTS CHANGED rather than what the runner printed: which newly pass, which newly fail, and which were ALREADY failing before the edit (labelled PRE-EXISTING). Raw runner output is never forwarded — ids are, text is not — and id lists cap at 20 with a count.

Record a baseline on the pristine tree first (--record-baseline), then pass that file as --pre-edit-baseline after editing. Without a baseline the verdict is a state rather than a delta, so a failure that predates the change cannot be labelled as one.

Parsers: pytest, jest/vitest, cargo test, go test, phpunit, rspec, minitest, maven/gradle surefire, ctest. An unrecognised format degrades to an exit-code-only verdict and says so.

Flags:
  --test <cmd>                 The test command to run (required)
  --repo <path>                Repository to run in (default: current repo)
  --setup <cmd>                Command run before the tests; its output never contributes test ids
  --record-baseline <path>     Write the pristine-tree result to this file instead of adjudicating
  --pre-edit-baseline <path>   Diff this run against a previously recorded baseline
  --max-bytes <n>              Cap the rendered verdict; the verdict clause always survives (default: 2048)

Examples:
  entire graph verify --repo . --test "pytest tests/test_parser.py" --record-baseline /tmp/base.json
  entire graph verify --repo . --test "pytest tests/test_parser.py" --pre-edit-baseline /tmp/base.json
---
Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Number of results to return (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file

input.content:
"""neatlogs setup. Every job is one trace; phases, tools and LLM calls are spans under it."""

import os

import neatlogs
from opentelemetry import trace as otel

AGENT_VERSION = os.environ.get("UPSHIFT_AGENT_VERSION", "v0")


def init(tags: list[str]) -> None:
    api_key = os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY")
    neatlogs.init(
        api_key=api_key,
        workflow_name="upshift",
        tags=[AGENT_VERSION, *tags],
        disable_export=not api_key,
    )


def annotate(**attrs) -> None:
    """Attach upshift.* attributes to the active span (state changes, failure class, retries)."""
    span = otel.get_current_span()
    for key, value in attrs.items():
        if value is not None:
            span.set_attribute(f"upshift.{key}", value if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) else str(value))


def shutdown() -> None:
    neatlogs.flush()
    neatlogs.shutdown()

"""Turn research into a cited migration playbook. Cached so the next repo skips research."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from . import tracing
from .llm import BedrockLLM, text_of, tool_result, tool_spec, tool_uses
from .research import fetch_text

CACHE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "playbooks"
MAX_TURNS = 10

SYSTEM = """You research Python dependency upgrades and write migration playbooks.

You get the package, the old and new versions, the project's doc and changelog pages, GitHub release
notes between the versions, and an API diff computed by installing both versions and comparing their
public symbols. The API diff is ground truth for what was removed or changed.

Read what you were given. If you need the official migration guide or a specific doc page, use
fetch_url (follow links you saw, don't guess random URLs). Then call submit_playbook once.

Each rule must describe one concrete breaking change a codebase could hit, as:
- old: the old usage, written as code
- new: what to write instead, as code
- detect: a Python regex that finds the old usage in source files, or "" if it can't be matched textually
- why: one sentence
- source: the URL you read it in, or "api-diff"
Only include rules supported by a source. Prefer 10-40 high-value rules over exhaustive lists."""

TOOLS = [
    tool_spec("fetch_url", "Fetch a web page as text (docs, migration guide, changelog).",
              {"url": {"type": "string"}}, ["url"]),
    tool_spec("submit_playbook", "Submit the finished playbook.", {
        "summary": {"type": "string", "description": "2-4 sentences on the shape of this upgrade."},
        "rules": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {
            "old": {"type": "string"}, "new": {"type": "string"}, "detect": {"type": "string"},
            "why": {"type": "string"}, "source": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["old", "new", "detect", "why", "source"]}},
    }, ["summary", "rules"]),
]


def cache_path(package: str, old: str, new: str) -> Path:
    return CACHE / f"{package.lower()}-{old}-{new}.json"


def load_cached(package: str, old: str, new: str) -> dict | None:
    path = cache_path(package, old, new)
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else None


def render_sources(sources: dict) -> str:
    docs = "\n\n".join(f"### {name}\n{text}" for name, text in sources["docs"].items())
    links = "\n".join(f"- {k}: {v}" for k, v in sources["links"].items())
    return (f"Package: {sources['package']}  {sources['old']} -> {sources['new']}\n\n"
            f"## Project links\n{links}\n\n## Doc and changelog pages\n{docs or '(none)'}\n\n"
            f"## GitHub release notes in range\n{sources['release_notes']}\n\n"
            f"## API diff (installed both versions)\n{sources['api_diff']}")


@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT", name="playbook")
def build(llm: BedrockLLM, sources: dict) -> dict:
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": render_sources(sources)}]}]
    fetched = 0
    for _ in range(MAX_TURNS):
        response = llm.converse(SYSTEM, messages, TOOLS, max_tokens=16000)
        message = response["output"]["message"]
        messages.append(message)
        uses = tool_uses(message)
        if not uses:
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Call submit_playbook with your rules."}]})
            continue
        results = []
        for use in uses:
            if use["name"] == "submit_playbook":
                playbook = {"package": sources["package"], "old": sources["old"], "new": sources["new"],
                            **use["input"]}
                tracing.annotate(playbook_rules=len(playbook["rules"]), urls_fetched=fetched)
                return playbook
            if use["name"] == "fetch_url":
                fetched += 1
                results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], fetch_text(use["input"]["url"])))
            else:
                results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], f"unknown tool {use['name']}", error=True))
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
    raise RuntimeError(f"no playbook after {MAX_TURNS} turns; last reply: {text_of(messages[-1])[:500]}")


def save(playbook: dict) -> Path:
    CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = cache_path(playbook["package"], playbook["old"], playbook["new"])
    path.write_text(json.dumps(playbook, indent=2))
    return path


def render(playbook: dict) -> str:
    lines = [playbook.get("summary", "")]
    for i, rule in enumerate(playbook["rules"], 1):
        lines.append(f"R{i}. {rule['old']}  =>  {rule['new']}   ({rule['why']}; source: {rule['source']})")
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""The fix loop: one root cause per round, tests after every round, commit progress, revert regressions."""

import re

import neatlogs
from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

from . import graph, tracing
from .llm import BedrockLLM, tool_result, tool_spec, tool_uses
from .playbook import render as render_playbook
from .research import fetch_text
from .state import RunState
from .workspace import TestRun, Workspace, tail

MAX_STEPS_PER_ROUND = 30
MAX_STALLS = 2

SYSTEM = """You are upgrading the Python package {package} from {old} to {new} in the repository at the
working directory. The new version is already installed and pinned. Your job is to change the code so the
test suite passes again. Tests that were already failing before the upgrade are not your concern.

Migration playbook (researched from the official docs, release notes and an API diff):
{playbook}

How to work in each round:
1. Read the failing output. Pick ONE root cause: the one behind the most failures.
2. Find every place in the codebase it occurs (search_code, graph_search, graph_impact), not just the
   line in the traceback.
3. Fix them with minimal edits that keep behaviour the same. Follow the playbook; if something isn't
   covered, use fetch_docs on the official docs.
4. Run the most relevant tests with run_tests, then call finish_round with a one-line summary.

Rules: don't edit dependency pins or lockfiles. Don't weaken, skip or delete tests. Don't silence
deprecation warnings instead of migrating. Paths are relative to the repo root."""

TOOLS = [
    tool_spec("read_file", "Read a file with line numbers. Optional 1-based start/end lines.",
              {"path": {"type": "string"}, "start": {"type": "integer"}, "end": {"type": "integer"}}, ["path"]),
    tool_spec("edit_file", "Replace one exact, unique occurrence of `old` with `new` in a file.",
              {"path": {"type": "string"}, "old": {"type": "string"}, "new": {"type": "string"}},
              ["path", "old", "new"]),
    tool_spec("search_code", "Regex search across the repo's source files. Returns path:line: text.",
              {"pattern": {"type": "string"}, "glob": {"type": "string", "description": "default *.py"}},
              ["pattern"]),
    tool_spec("run_tests", "Run pytest. `selector` is passed through, e.g. 'tests/test_models.py -k parse'.",
              {"selector": {"type": "string"}}, []),
    tool_spec("graph_search", "entire-graph: find code for a plain-language description, ranked with context.",
              {"query": {"type": "string"}}, ["query"]),
    tool_spec("graph_impact", "entire-graph: callers, callees and related files for a symbol.",
              {"symbol": {"type": "string"}}, ["symbol"]),
    tool_spec("graph_explain", "entire-graph: resolve the symbols named in a failure (paste the error).",
              {"failure": {"type": "string"}}, ["failure"]),
    tool_spec("lookup_playbook", "Find playbook rules mentioning any of these words.",
              {"query": {"type": "string"}}, ["query"]),
    tool_spec("fetch_docs", "Fetch a documentation page as text.", {"url": {"type": "string"}}, ["url"]),
    tool_spec("finish_round", "End this round once the root cause is fixed everywhere.",
              {"summary": {"type": "string"}}, ["summary"]),
]


class FixLoop:
    def __init__(self, ws: Workspace, llm: BedrockLLM, state: RunState, playbook: dict, max_rounds: int = 12):
        self.ws, self.llm, self.state, self.playbook = ws, llm, state, playbook
        self.max_rounds = max_rounds
        self.baseline = set(state.baseline_failing)
        self.system = SYSTEM.format(package=state.package, old=state.old, new=state.new,
                                    playbook=render_playbook(playbook))

    def new_failures(self, run: TestRun) -> set[str]:
        return run.failing - self.baseline

    def run(self, save) -> TestRun:
        current = self.ws.run_tests()
        stalls = 0
        while self.state.round < self.max_rounds:
            if not self.new_failures(current) and current.exit_code in (0, 1, 5):
                break
            self.state.round += 1
            current, outcome = self.one_round(self.state.round, current)
            save()
            stalls = stalls + 1 if outcome != "progress" else 0
            if stalls >= MAX_STALLS:
                self.state.notes.append(f"stopped after {stalls} rounds without progress")
                break
        return current

    def one_round(self, n: int, before: TestRun) -> tuple[TestRun, str]:
        with neatlogs.trace(f"fix.{n}", kind="AGENT") as span:
            failing = sorted(self.new_failures(before))
            prompt = (f"Round {n}. {len(failing)} tests fail that passed before the upgrade "
                      f"({before.passed} passing now).\nFailing: {', '.join(failing[:40])}\n\n"
                      f"Previous rounds:\n" + ("\n".join(self.state.round_log) or "(none)") +
                      f"\n\nPytest output:\n{tail(before.output, 10000)}")
            try:
                summary = self.converse(prompt)
            except ClientError as exc:
                code = exc.response.get("Error", {}).get("Code", "ClientError")
                tracing.annotate(failure_class=f"llm:{code}", recovery="revert_and_retry_next_round")
                self.ws.git("checkout", "--", ".")
                self.ws.git("clean", "-fdq")
                self.state.round_log.append(f"round {n}: model call failed ({code}); changes reverted")
                return before, "error"

            after = self.ws.run_tests()
            new_before, new_after = self.new_failures(before), self.new_failures(after)
            if after.passed < before.passed and len(new_after) >= len(new_before):
                outcome = "regression"
                self.ws.git("checkout", "--", ".")
                self.ws.git("clean", "-fdq")
                tracing.annotate(failure_class="test_regression", recovery="revert_and_replan")
                self.state.round_log.append(
                    f"round {n}: REVERTED. '{summary}' made things worse "
                    f"({before.passed} -> {after.passed} passing). Try a different approach.")
                after = before
            elif self.ws.git("status", "--porcelain").strip() and (
                    after.passed > before.passed or len(new_after) < len(new_before)):
                outcome = "progress"
                self.ws.git("add", "-A")
                self.ws.git("commit", "-q", "-m", f"upshift: {summary}"[:200])
                self.state.round_log.append(
                    f"round {n}: {summary} ({before.passed} -> {after.passed} passing, "
                    f"{len(new_after)} new failures left)")
            else:
                outcome = "stall"
                self.state.round_log.append(f"round {n}: no measurable progress. '{summary}'")
            span.set_attribute("upshift.outcome", outcome)
            span.set_attribute("upshift.passed_before", before.passed)
            span.set_attribute("upshift.passed_after", after.passed)
            span.set_attribute("upshift.new_failures_left", len(self.new_failures(after)))
            return after, outcome

    def converse(self, prompt: str) -> str:
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": prompt}]}]
        for _ in range(MAX_STEPS_PER_ROUND):
            response = self.llm.converse(self.system, messages, TOOLS)
            message = response["output"]["message"]
            messages.append(message)
            uses = tool_uses(message)
            if not uses:
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Continue with tools, or call finish_round."}]})
                continue
            results, finished = [], None
            for use in uses:
                if use["name"] == "finish_round":
                    finished = use["input"].get("summary", "").strip() or "round finished"
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], "ok"))
                    continue
                try:
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], self.call_tool(use["name"], use["input"])))
                except Exception as exc:  # tool errors go back to the model so it can recover
                    tracing.annotate(failure_class=f"tool:{use['name']}", recovery="returned_to_model")
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", error=True))
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
            if finished:
                return finished
        tracing.annotate(failure_class="step_budget", recovery="end_round")
        return "step budget for the round ran out"

    def call_tool(self, name: str, args: dict) -> str:
        ws = self.ws
        if name == "read_file":
            lines = ws.resolve(args["path"]).read_text().splitlines()
            start = max(args.get("start") or 1, 1)
            end = min(args.get("end") or start + 399, len(lines), start + 399)
            return "\n".join(f"{i:5}  {lines[i - 1]}" for i in range(start, end + 1)) or "(empty file)"
        if name == "edit_file":
            return edit_file(ws, args["path"], args["old"], args["new"])
        if name == "search_code":
            return search_code(ws, args["pattern"], args.get("glob") or "*.py")
        if name == "run_tests":
            run = ws.run_tests(args.get("selector", ""))
            return f"{run.summary}\n{tail(run.output, 6000)}"
        if name == "graph_search":
            return tail(graph.search(str(ws.repo), args["query"]), 16000)
        if name == "graph_impact":
            return tail(graph.impact(str(ws.repo), args["symbol"]), 8000)
        if name == "graph_explain":
            return tail(graph.explain(str(ws.repo), args["failure"]), 8000)
        if name == "lookup_playbook":
            words = [w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\w+", args["query"]) if len(w) > 2]
            hits = [r for r in self.playbook["rules"]
                    if any(w in (r["old"] + r["new"] + r["why"]).lower() for w in words)]
            return "\n".join(f"{r['old']} => {r['new']} ({r['why']}; {r['source']})" for r in hits[:20]) or "no matching rules"
        if name == "fetch_docs":
            return fetch_text(args["url"], cap=20000)
        raise ValueError(f"unknown tool {name}")


@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="edit_file")
def edit_file(ws: Workspace, path: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
    target = ws.resolve(path)
    text = target.read_text()
    count = text.count(old)
    if count != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"`old` matched {count} times in {path}; it must match exactly once. "
                         "Re-read the file and include more surrounding lines.")
    target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))
    return f"edited {path}"


@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="search_code")
def search_code(ws: Workspace, pattern: str, glob: str = "*.py", limit: int = 80) -> str:
    regex = re.compile(pattern)
    hits = []
    for path in sorted(ws.source_files()):
        if not path.match(glob):
            continue
        try:
            lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            if regex.search(line):
                hits.append(f"{path.relative_to(ws.repo)}:{i}: {line.strip()[:200]}")
                if len(hits) >= limit:
                    return "\n".join(hits) + f"\n...[stopped at {limit} matches]"
    return "\n".join(hits) or "no matches"

"""Run state, saved after every step so a crashed or killed run can resume."""

import json
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".upshift" / "runs"
PHASES = ["setup", "baseline", "research", "bump", "fix", "verify", "report", "done"]


@dataclass
class RunState:
    run_id: str
    kind: str              # bump | vuln | python | api
    source: str            # repo path or URL
    package: str
    wanted: str | None     # what the user asked for, e.g. "2"
    python: str = "3.12"
    phase: str = "setup"
    old: str = ""
    new: str = ""
    baseline_failing: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    baseline_passed: int = 0
    playbook_path: str = ""
    round: int = 0
    round_log: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    result: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0

    @property
    def dir(self) -> Path:
        return RUNS / self.run_id

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.dir / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps(asdict(self), indent=2))

    def advance(self, phase: str) -> None:
        self.phase = phase
        self.save()

    def reached(self, phase: str) -> bool:
        """True when `phase` already completed in an earlier attempt."""
        return PHASES.index(self.phase) > PHASES.index(phase)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, run_id: str) -> "RunState":
        return cls(**json.loads((RUNS / run_id / "state.json").read_text()))

"""One job end to end: setup → baseline → research → bump → fix → verify → report.

Each phase is a neatlogs span under the job's WORKFLOW trace, and state is saved between phases.
"""

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs
from packaging.version import Version

from . import graph, playbook, research, tracing
from .agent import FixLoop
from .llm import BedrockLLM
from .state import RunState
from .workspace import Workspace

REPORT = "UPSHIFT_REPORT.md"


class Stop(Exception):
    """Ends the job early with a message (already at target, dry run, ...)."""


def run(state: RunState, dry_run: bool = False) -> RunState:
    ws = Workspace(state.dir, python=state.python)
    llm = None if dry_run else BedrockLLM()
    with neatlogs.identify(session_id=state.run_id):
        with neatlogs.trace(f"upshift.{state.kind}", kind="WORKFLOW") as root:
            root.set_attribute("upshift.package", state.package)
            root.set_attribute("upshift.repo", state.source)
            root.set_attribute("upshift.run_id", state.run_id)
            try:
                for phase in ("setup", "baseline", "research", "bump", "fix", "verify", "report"):
                    if state.reached(phase):
                        continue
                    with neatlogs.trace(phase, kind="AGENT"):
                        PHASES[phase](state, ws, llm, dry_run)
                    state.advance(next_phase(phase))
                    print(f"[upshift] {phase} done")
            except Stop as stop:
                state.notes.append(str(stop))
                print(f"[upshift] stopped: {stop}")
            finally:
                if llm:
                    state.input_tokens, state.output_tokens = llm.input_tokens, llm.output_tokens
                root.set_attribute("upshift.phase_reached", state.phase)
                state.save()
    return state


def next_phase(phase: str) -> str:
    order = ["setup", "baseline", "research", "bump", "fix", "verify", "report", "done"]
    return order[order.index(phase) + 1]


def setup(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    info = research.pypi_info(state.package)
    state.new = research.resolve_target(info, state.wanted)
    if not ws.repo.exists():
        ws.clone(state.source, f"upshift/{state.kind}-{state.package}-{state.new}")
    ws.install()
    state.old = ws.installed_version(state.package) or ""
    tracing.annotate(old=state.old, new=state.new)
    if not state.old:
        raise Stop(f"{state.package} is not installed by this project")
    if Version(state.old) >= Version(state.new):
        raise Stop(f"{state.package} is already at {state.old} (target {state.new})")


def baseline(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    run = ws.run_tests()
    state.baseline_failing = sorted(run.failing)
    state.baseline_passed = run.passed
    graph.verify(str(ws.repo), ws.test_cmd, record_baseline=str(state.dir / "verify-baseline.json"))
    tracing.annotate(baseline_passed=run.passed, baseline_failing=len(run.failing))


def do_research(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    cached = playbook.load_cached(state.package, state.old, state.new)
    if cached:
        state.playbook_path = str(playbook.cache_path(state.package, state.old, state.new))
        tracing.annotate(playbook_cache="hit")
        return
    tracing.annotate(playbook_cache="miss")
    sources = research.gather(state.package, state.old, state.new, state.python, state.dir)
    (state.dir / "sources.md").write_text(playbook.render_sources(sources))
    if dry_run:
        return
    state.playbook_path = str(playbook.save(playbook.build(llm, sources)))


def bump(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    ws.set_version(state.package, state.new)
    ws.git("add", "-A")
    ws.git("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", f"upshift: bump {state.package} {state.old} -> {state.new}")
    if dry_run:
        run = ws.run_tests()
        new = sorted(run.failing - set(state.baseline_failing))
        (state.dir / "after-bump.txt").write_text(run.output)
        raise Stop(f"dry run: after the bump {run.passed} pass, {len(new)} new failures "
                   f"(sources in {state.dir / 'sources.md'}, pytest output in {state.dir / 'after-bump.txt'})")


def fix(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    pb = json.loads(Path(state.playbook_path).read_text())
    FixLoop(ws, llm, state, pb).run(state.save)


def verify(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    run = ws.run_tests()
    new_failures = sorted(run.failing - set(state.baseline_failing))
    verdict = graph.verify(str(ws.repo), ws.test_cmd, pre_edit_baseline=str(state.dir / "verify-baseline.json"))
    pb = json.loads(Path(state.playbook_path).read_text())
    leftovers = leftover_usages(ws, pb)
    state.result = {
        "passed": run.passed,
        "baseline_passed": state.baseline_passed,
        "new_failures": new_failures,
        "leftover_old_apis": leftovers,
        "entire_verdict": verdict,
        "ok": not new_failures,
    }
    tracing.annotate(ok=not new_failures, new_failures=len(new_failures), leftovers=len(leftovers))


def leftover_usages(ws: Workspace, pb: dict, limit: int = 50) -> list[str]:
    hits = []
    patterns = []
    for rule in pb["rules"]:
        try:
            patterns.append((re.compile(rule["detect"]), rule["old"])) if rule.get("detect") else None
        except re.error:
            continue
    for path in ws.source_files():
        if path.suffix != ".py":
            continue
        for i, line in enumerate(path.read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines(), 1):
            for regex, old in patterns:
                if regex.search(line):
                    hits.append(f"{path.relative_to(ws.repo)}:{i}  ({old})")
                    if len(hits) >= limit:
                        return hits
    return hits


def report(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    r = state.result
    pb = json.loads(Path(state.playbook_path).read_text())
    diffstat = ws.git("diff", "--stat", f"HEAD~{max(1, len(state.round_log))}", "HEAD").strip().splitlines()
    lines = [
        f"# Upshift: {state.package} {state.old} → {state.new}",
        "",
        f"**Result:** {'no new test failures' if r['ok'] else str(len(r['new_failures'])) + ' new test failures remain'}"
        f" · {r['passed']} passing (baseline {r['baseline_passed']})",
        f"**Run:** `{state.run_id}` · {state.round} fix rounds · "
        f"{state.input_tokens:,} input / {state.output_tokens:,} output tokens",
        "",
        "## What changed",
        *[f"- {entry}" for entry in state.round_log],
        "",
        f"`{diffstat[-1].strip() if diffstat else 'no diff'}`",
        "",
        "## Verification (entire graph verify against the pre-upgrade baseline)",
        "```", r["entire_verdict"].strip(), "```",
    ]
    if r["new_failures"]:
        lines += ["", "## Still failing", *[f"- `{t}`" for t in r["new_failures"]]]
    if r["leftover_old_apis"]:
        lines += ["", "## Old APIs still in use", *[f"- {h}" for h in r["leftover_old_apis"]]]
    lines += ["", "## Playbook", pb.get("summary", ""), "",
              *[f"- `{x['old']}` → `{x['new']}` — {x['why']} ([source]({x['source']}))"
                if x["source"].startswith("http") else f"- `{x['old']}` → `{x['new']}` — {x['why']} (API diff)"
                for x in pb["rules"]]]
    if state.notes:
        lines += ["", "## Notes", *[f"- {n}" for n in state.notes]]
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    (ws.repo / REPORT).write_text(text)
    (state.dir / REPORT).write_text(text)
    ws.git("add", REPORT)
    ws.git("commit", "-q", "-m", f"upshift: report for {state.package} {state.new}")

"""upshift bump --repo PATH_OR_URL --package NAME [--to VERSION]
upshift resume RUN_ID"""

import argparse
import sys
import time

from . import pipeline, tracing
from .llm import LLMConfigError
from .state import RunState


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="upshift", description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    bump = sub.add_parser("bump", help="upgrade a package and fix what breaks")
    bump.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="local path or git URL")
    bump.add_argument("--package", required=True)
    bump.add_argument("--to", help="target version or prefix (default: latest stable)")
    bump.add_argument("--python", default="3.12", help="Python for the project's venv")
    bump.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                      help="no model calls: set up, baseline, gather research, bump, show what breaks")

    resume = sub.add_parser("resume", help="continue a run from its last completed phase")
    resume.add_argument("run_id")
    resume.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "bump":
        run_id = f"{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}-{args.package.lower()}"
        state = RunState(run_id=run_id, kind="bump", source=args.repo, package=args.package,
                         wanted=args.to, python=args.python)
        state.save()
    else:
        state = RunState.load(args.run_id)

    tracing.init([state.kind, state.package])
    print(f"[upshift] run {state.run_id} → {state.dir}")
    try:
        state = pipeline.run(state, dry_run=args.dry_run)
    except LLMConfigError as exc:
        print(f"[upshift] {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    finally:
        tracing.shutdown()
    if state.result:
        print(f"[upshift] {'OK' if state.result['ok'] else 'INCOMPLETE'}: "
              f"{state.result['passed']} passing, {len(state.result['new_failures'])} new failures. "
              f"Report: {state.dir / pipeline.REPORT}")
    return 0 if state.result.get("ok") or args.dry_run else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import itertools

import pytest

from upshift.agent import FixLoop
from upshift.state import RunState
from upshift.workspace import Workspace

PLAYBOOK = {"summary": "test", "rules": [
    {"old": "add(a, b) returns a - b", "new": "return a + b", "detect": "", "why": "bug", "source": "api-diff"}]}


class ScriptedLLM:
    """Returns one canned assistant message per converse() call."""

    def __init__(self, *messages):
        self.messages = iter(messages)
        self.ids = itertools.count()
        self.input_tokens = self.output_tokens = 0

    def converse(self, system, messages, tools=None, max_tokens=8000):
        return {"output": {"message": next(self.messages)}}

    def call(self, name, **args):
        return {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"toolUse": {"toolUseId": f"t{next(self.ids)}", "name": name, "input": args}}]}


@pytest.fixture
def workspace(tmp_path):
    src = tmp_path / "src"
    (src / "tests").mkdir(parents=True)
    (src / "calc.py").write_text("def add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n\n\ndef neg(a):\n    return -a\n")
    (src / "tests" / "test_calc.py").write_text(
        "from calc import add, neg\n\n\ndef test_add():\n    assert add(2, 3) == 5\n\n\n"
        "def test_neg():\n    assert neg(2) == -2\n")
    (src / "conftest.py").write_text("")
    ws = Workspace(tmp_path / "run", python="3.12")
    ws.clone(str(src), "upshift/test")
    ws.install()
    return ws


def state_for(ws):
    return RunState(run_id="test", kind="bump", source="x", package="calc", wanted=None,
                    old="1", new="2", baseline_failing=[])


def test_progress_is_committed(workspace):
    llm = ScriptedLLM()
    llm.messages = iter([
        llm.call("edit_file", path="calc.py", old="return a - b", new="return a + b"),
        llm.call("finish_round", summary="fix add"),
    ])

    final = FixLoop(workspace, llm, state, PLAYBOOK, max_rounds=3).run(lambda: None)
    assert not final.failing

    assert "fix add" in workspace.git("log", "-1", "--format=%s")


def test_regression_is_reverted(workspace):
    llm = ScriptedLLM()
    llm.messages = iter([
        # round 1 "fixes" add but breaks neg -> fewer passing overall? no: 1 passing before, 1 after.
        # make it strictly worse: break neg and leave add broken
        llm.call("edit_file", path="calc.py", old="return -a", new="return a"),
        llm.call("finish_round", summary="bad change"),
        llm.call("edit_file", path="calc.py", old="return a - b", new="return a + b"),
        llm.call("finish_round", summary="fix add"),
    ])
    state = state_for(workspace)
    final = FixLoop(workspace, llm, state, PLAYBOOK, max_rounds=3).run(lambda: None)
    assert "REVERTED" in state.round_log[0]
    assert not final.failing
    assert "return -a" in (workspace.repo / "calc.py").read_text()


def test_bad_edit_goes_back_to_the_model(workspace):
    llm = ScriptedLLM()
    llm.messages = iter([
        llm.call("edit_file", path="calc.py", old="does not exist", new="x"),
        llm.call("edit_file", path="calc.py", old="return a - b", new="return a + b"),
        llm.call("finish_round", summary="fix add after retry"),
    ])
    state = state_for(workspace)
    final = FixLoop(workspace, llm, state, PLAYBOOK, max_rounds=2).run(lambda: None)
    assert not final.failing

# upshift

Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass.

Upshift is an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. Give it a Python repo and a package to
upgrade. It researches the upgrade itself (changelog, release notes, migration guide, and an API diff
made by installing both versions), writes a playbook where every rule cites its source, bumps the
dependency, fixes the code one root cause at a time, and proves nothing new broke against the test
baseline it recorded before touching anything.

Built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Claude runs on Amazon Bedrock.

## Status

Day 1: the package-bump pipeline works end to end with model calls stubbed out (Bedrock access is
pending). Vulnerability scans, Python version bumps and third-party API drift come next.

## Run it

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env   # fill in, then: set -a; source .env; set +a

# no model calls: clone, baseline, research, bump, and show what breaks
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2 --dry-run

# the full agent
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2
uv run upshift resume <run-id>     # continue a crashed or killed run
```

Runs live in `.upshift/runs/<run-id>/`: the working copy, its venv, `state.json`, the research sources and
the report. Playbooks are cached in `playbooks/` and reused by the next repo on the same upgrade.

## How a job runs

| Phase | What happens | Where the tools come in |
|---|---|---|
| setup | Clone, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI | |
| baseline | Run the tests before changing anything | `entire graph verify --record-baseline` |
| research | Docs, changelog, GitHub release notes, API diff of both installed versions → cited playbook | neatlogs `RETRIEVER`/`AGENT` spans |
| bump | Rewrite the pins and install the new version | |
| fix | One root cause per round. Progress is committed, regressions are reverted | `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools, one neatlogs span per round |
| verify | No new failures against the baseline, no old APIs left from the playbook | `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` |
| report | `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with changes, verification and sources | |

Every job is one neatlogs trace. Bedrock calls are traced by wrapping the boto3 client with `neatlogs.wrap`.

## Tests

```bash
uv run pytest
```

The fix-loop tests drive the real loop (repo, venv, pytest, git) with a scripted model in place of Bedrock.

"""Pre-commit guard: refuse commits that stage a .env file or contain an API key.

Install once per clone:  python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --install
It checks the staged diff for (1) any .env file other than .env.example, (2) the actual values of
secret-looking variables from .env and the environment, (3) common key formats.
Matches are reported by file and line, never by value.
"""

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SECRET_NAME = re.compile(r"KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL", re.I)
KEY_FORMATS = [
    re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"),                    # OpenAI-style
    re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"),                # Anthropic
    re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),                          # AWS access key id
    re.compile(r"(?i)(api[_-]?key|secret|token)\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?[A-Za-z0-9/+_\-]{24,}"),
]
HOOK = """#!/bin/sh
# upshift: block commits that contain secrets
python3 "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/scripts/check_secrets.py" || exit 1
"""


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def secret_values() -> set[str]:
    values = {v for k, v in os.environ.items() if SECRET_NAME.search(k) and len(v) >= 12}
    env_file = Path(git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel").strip()) / ".env"
    if env_file.exists():
        for line in env_file.read_text().splitlines():
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            value = value.strip().strip("\"'")
            if SECRET_NAME.search(key) and len(value) >= 12:
                values.add(value)
    return values


def main() -> int:
    if "--install" in sys.argv:
        hook = Path(git("rev-parse", "--git-path", "hooks").strip()) / "pre-commit"
        hook.write_text(HOOK)
        hook.chmod(0o755)
        print(f"installed {hook}")
        return 0

    problems = []
    for name in git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=ACMR").splitlines():
        base = Path(name).name
        if base == ".env" or (base.startswith(".env.") and base != ".env.example"):
            problems.append(f"{name}: .env files must never be committed")

    values = secret_values()
    current = None
    for line in git("diff", "--cached", "-U0", "--no-color").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            current = line[6:]
            continue
        if not line.startswith("+") or line.startswith("+++"):
            continue
        added = line[1:]
        if any(v in added for v in values):
            problems.append(f"{current}: contains the value of a secret from your environment or .env")
        elif any(p.search(added) for p in KEY_FORMATS):
            problems.append(f"{current}: looks like an API key")

    if problems:
        print("Commit blocked, possible secrets staged:", file=sys.stderr)
        for p in sorted(set(problems)):
            print(f"  - {p}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Unstage them (git restore --staged <file>) and keep keys in .env.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import pytest

from upshift.llm import LLMConfigError, from_openai, make_llm, openai_tool, to_openai, tool_result, tool_spec


def test_tool_spec_becomes_openai_function():
    spec = tool_spec("read_file", "Read a file.", {"path": {"type": "string"}}, ["path"])
    assert openai_tool(spec) == {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "read_file", "description": "Read a file.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}}


def test_conversation_round_trip_to_openai():
    messages = [
        {"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "fix it"}]},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"text": "reading"},
            {"toolUse": {"toolUseId": "c1", "name": "read_file", "input": {"path": "a.py"}}}]},
        {"role": "user", "content": [tool_result("c1", "no such file", error=True)]},
    ]
    assert to_openai("sys", messages) == [
        {"role": "system", "content": "sys"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "fix it"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "reading", "tool_calls": [
            {"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": '{"path": "a.py"}'}}]},

v1 is done, with a measured improvement from the trace. Read on the same demo app and model, it costs 17% less ($0.396 → $0.327), uses 26% fewer tokens (193K → 142K), and leaves no deprecated calls, down from 6. Both runs still finish with 16/16 tests passing and no test files touched.

**How neatlogs drove it:** I read the v0 trace through the neatlogs MCP server (`search_traces`, `get_trace_context`). It showed:
- **Duplicate fetches during research:** the model fetched the Pydantic migration page 11 times with different `#anchor`s. Every fetch returned the same 30 KB page, and all of it went into the next model call.
- **A growing fix-loop history:** each of the 10 fix-loop calls resent the whole conversation, including pytest's warnings section every time.
- **A "Slow LLM Response" detection** on the 38-second research call.

**What changed in v1 (20 tests pass):**
- **One fetch per page:** pages are fetched once per conversation, and `#anchor` variants are refused with a short note. v1 made 0 duplicate fetches.
- **Smaller history:** tool outputs older than the last two steps are shortened, and the pytest warnings section is stripped.
- **Cleanup round:** once tests pass, the agent tries to migrate deprecated calls that remain. It commits only if tests still pass and the count drops; otherwise it reverts.
- **Per-round token counts** are now recorded on each fix and cleanup span in neatlogs.
- **`--fresh-research`** makes the comparison fair, since v1 didn't reuse v0's cached research.

**Limits of this evidence:**
- **One run each.** Model output varies between runs, so part of the difference could be luck. Repeating both versions on a few real open-source repos would make the claim solid.
- **The cleanup round never ran for real.** In v1 the model happened to migrate `orders.py` in its first fix round, so cleanup had nothing to do. Only the tests with a scripted model exercise it so far.
- **v0's code exists nowhere now.** Nothing is committed, so v0 can't be re-run for more comparisons. Committing locally now would preserve v1, and doesn't push anything.

Both trace IDs and the full comparison table are in `hackathon.md`. In the neatlogs dashboard, the runs are tagged `v0` and `v1`.

70	class FixLoop:
71	    def __init__(self, ws: Workspace, llm, state: RunState, playbook: dict, max_rounds: int = 12):
72	        self.ws, self.llm, self.state, self.playbook = ws, llm, state, playbook
73	        self.max_rounds = max_rounds

76	        self.system = SYSTEM.format(package=state.package, old=state.old, new=state.new,
77	                                    playbook=render_playbook(playbook))

79	    def new_failures(self, run: TestRun) -> set[str]:
80	        return run.failing - self.baseline

82	    def run(self, save) -> TestRun:
83	        current = self.ws.run_tests()
84	        stalls = 0
85	        while self.state.round < self.max_rounds:
86	            if not self.new_failures(current) and current.exit_code in (0, 1, 5):
87	                break
88	            self.state.round += 1
89	            current, outcome = self.one_round(self.state.round, current)
90	            save()

92	            if stalls >= MAX_STALLS:
93	                self.state.notes.append(f"stopped after {stalls} rounds without progress")
94	                break

97	    def one_round(self, n: int, before: TestRun) -> tuple[TestRun, str]:
98	        with neatlogs.trace(f"fix.{n}", kind="AGENT") as span:

104	                      f"\n\nPytest output:\n{failure_digest(before.output)}")
105	            try:
106	                summary = self.converse(prompt)

110	                self.revert()

112	                return before, "error"

116	            if after.passed < before.passed and len(new_after) >= len(new_before):

146	    def cleanup(self, find_leftovers, save) -> None:
147	        """Tests pass; now migrate deprecated calls that still work but will break later.

149	        v0 stopped as soon as tests passed and left six deprecated calls behind.

192	    def converse(self, prompt: str) -> str:
193	        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": prompt}]}]
194	        for _ in range(MAX_STEPS_PER_ROUND):
195	            compact(messages)
196	            response = self.llm.converse(self.system, messages, TOOLS)
197	            message = response["output"]["message"]
198	            messages.append(message)
199	            uses = tool_uses(message)
200	            if not uses:
201	                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Continue with tools, or call finish_round."}]})
202	                continue
203	            results, finished = [], None
204	            for use in uses:
205	                if "_invalid_json" in use["input"]:
206	                    tracing.annotate(failure_class="tool_args_invalid_json", recovery="returned_to_model")
207	                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], "Your tool arguments were not valid JSON. "
208	                                               "Call the tool again with valid JSON.", error=True))
209	                    continue
210	                if use["name"] == "finish_round":
211	                    finished = use["input"].get("summary", "").strip() or "round finished"
212	                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], "ok"))
213	                    continue
214	                try:
215	                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], self.call_tool(use["name"], use["input"])))
216	                except Exception as exc:  # tool errors go back to the model so it can recover
217	                    tracing.annotate(failure_class=f"tool:{use['name']}", recovery="returned_to_model")
218	                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", error=True))
219	            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
220	            if finished:
221	                return finished
222	        tracing.annotate(failure_class="step_budget", recovery="end_round")
223	        return "step budget for the round ran out"

225	    def call_tool(self, name: str, args: dict) -> str:
226	        ws = self.ws
227	        if name == "read_file":
228	            lines = ws.resolve(args["path"]).read_text().splitlines()
229	            start = max(args.get("start") or 1, 1)
230	            end = min(args.get("end") or start + 399, len(lines), start + 399)
231	            return "\n".join(f"{i:5}  {lines[i - 1]}" for i in range(start, end + 1)) or "(empty file)"
232	        if name == "edit_file":
233	            return edit_file(ws, args["path"], args["old"], args["new"])
234	        if name == "search_code":
235	            return search_code(ws, args["pattern"], args.get("glob") or "*.py")
236	        if name == "run_tests":
237	            run = ws.run_tests(args.get("selector", ""))
238	            return f"{run.summary}\n{failure_digest(run.output, 5000)}"
239	        if name == "graph_search":
240	            return tail(graph.search(str(ws.repo), args["query"]), 16000)
241	        if name == "graph_impact":
242	            return tail(graph.impact(str(ws.repo), args["symbol"]), 8000)
243	        if name == "graph_explain":
244	            return tail(graph.explain(str(ws.repo), args["failure"]), 8000)
245	        if name == "lookup_playbook":
246	            words = [w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\w+", args["query"]) if len(w) > 2]
247	            hits = [r for r in self.playbook["rules"]
248	                    if any(w in (r["old"] + r["new"] + r["why"]).lower() for w in words)]
249	            return "\n".join(f"{r['old']} => {r['new']} ({r['why']}; {r['source']})" for r in hits[:20]) or "no matching rules"
250	        if name == "fetch_docs":
251	            return self.fetch(args["url"])
252	        raise ValueError(f"unknown tool {name}")

255	WARNINGS_SECTION = re.compile(r"^=+ warnings summary =+$.*?(?=^=+ |^\d+ \w+|\Z)", re.S | re.M)
256	
257	
258	def failure_digest(output: str, limit: int = 6000) -> str:
259	    """Pytest output without the warnings summary, which in v0 repeated on every round."""
260	    return tail(WARNINGS_SECTION.sub("[warnings summary omitted]\n", output), limit)
261	
262	
263	def compact(messages: list[dict]) -> None:
264	    """Shorten tool results older than the last few steps; each model call resends the whole history."""
265	    result_turns = [m for m in messages if m["role"] == "user" and any("toolResult" in b for b in m["content"])]
266	    for message in result_turns[:-KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS]:
267	        for block in message["content"]:
268	            for part in block.get("toolResult", {}).get("content", []):
269	                text = part.get("text", "")
270	                if len(text) > ELIDE_OVER:
271	                    part["text"] = (text[:500] + f"\n...[{len(text) - 500} chars from an earlier step elided; "
272	                                    "call the tool again if you need them]")
273

275	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="edit_file")
276	def edit_file(ws: Workspace, path: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
277	    target = ws.resolve(path)
278	    text = target.read_text()
279	    count = text.count(old)
280	    if count != 1:
281	        raise ValueError(f"`old` matched {count} times in {path}; it must match exactly once. "
282	                         "Re-read the file and include more surrounding lines.")
283	    target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))
284	    return f"edited {path}"
285	
286	
287	@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="search_code")
288	def search_code(ws: Workspace, pattern: str, glob: str = "*.py", limit: int = 80) -> str:
289	    regex = re.compile(pattern)
290	    hits = []
291	    for path in sorted(ws.source_files()):
292	        if not path.match(glob):
293	            continue
294	        try:
295	            lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
296	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
297	            continue
298	        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
299	            if regex.search(line):
300	                hits.append(f"{path.relative_to(ws.repo)}:{i}: {line.strip()[:200]}")
301	                if len(hits) >= limit:
302	                    return "\n".join(hits) + f"\n...[stopped at {limit} matches]"
303	    return "\n".join(hits) or "no matches"
